body:
oncall-bot: Monitoring alert: sudden spike in 502s from eu2 gateway cluster, detected 2143587598-2143587600 window

maria.sre: saw the same on dashboard, p50 latency okay but p95 -> large, errors up ~18% over last 5m :warning:

kevin.neteng: is this across all AZs in eu2 or a single AZ?

maria.sre: looks concentrated to eu2-azb, cross-zone requests hitting gateway show timeouts and upstream closed connection logs.

priya.support: we just had an Enterprise support ticket (ACME Corp) complaining about streaming disconnects and auth errors. Ticket #SUP-1423. They reported reconnects every ~30s during long inference streams.

sam.runtime: interesting — long-lived streaming sessions + intermittent 502s could be TCP-level loss or TLS renegotiation killing connections. Any packet-reordering visible?

alex.infra: pulling logs from gateway: example from 2143587601

```
[proxy] 2026-03-15T08:26:41Z upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.4.82.12, server: api.eu2.redwood, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.9.4.21:8080/", host: "api.eu2.redwood"
```

kevin.neteng: running mtr from eu2-edge to provider next-hop now, will paste results.

kevin.neteng: mtr summary (truncated):
```
 1. 10.1.0.1    0.2% loss
 2. 203.0.113.5 0.0% loss
 3. 198.51.100.7 12.3% loss, high rta variance
 4. 198.51.100.11 11.8% loss, AS64500
 5. 198.51.200.2  0.0% loss
```

kevin.neteng: see the micro-loss and high jitter across the transit hop (AS64500). matches the times of errors.

maria.sre: tcpdump sampled on gateway shows a burst of retransmits and out-of-order packets, then the connection resets. snippet:
```
15:26:41.123456 IP srv > client: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12567, ack 23456, win 64240
15:26:41.123789 IP client > srv: Flags [.], ack 12567, seq 23456, win 65535
15:26:41.124001 IP srv > client: [TCP Retransmission] Flags [P.], seq 12345:12567 ...
15:26:41.124500 IP srv > client: RST, seq 12567
```

priya.support: ACME attached a curl repro that fails after ~30s. they were doing streaming with `--http2` and a keepalive token that refreshes on the client side.

sam.runtime: reproduce steps I ran:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST https://api.eu2.redwood/v1/chat/stream -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"long story"}],"stream":true}' --http2
```
Result: stream opens, gets ~25-40s of tokens then connection drops with HTTP/2 rst_stream 0x8 and gateway returns 502.

alex.infra: I see also a small spike in auth-service 5xxs at same time, likely cascading because our token validation upstream hits timeouts waiting on responses from runtime nodes that got reset.

kevin.neteng: contacted transit provider NOC (ticket TG-789) — they acknowledged microbursts on one aggregation circuit at their EU POP between 08:25-08:40 UTC, saw asymmetric path changes and brief partial withdrawals. They are doing a fiber re-provisioning and will escalate to engineering.

maria.sre: mitigation options: 1) traffic steering to eu2-edge-b pool in different POP, 2) enable temporary retry/backoff on gateway to smooth transient resets, 3) ask support to pause long-lived session tests for affected customers while we mitigate. Which do we prefer?

sam.runtime: prefer steering + retry. Steering reduces exposure quickly. I'll prepare a runtime-side soft retry that preserves streaming state where possible (up to 2 re-attempts within 5s).

alex.infra: I can push a traffic policy to route new sessions away from the affected aggregation (eu2-agg-b) to eu2-agg-a. doing a gradual 60% shift now. deploy-bot: Starting rollout of route-adjustment policy eu2-shift-2143587600 (canary 10% -> 60%).

oncall-bot: Rollout 2143587600 queued and applied to edge-router cluster eu2 in 3 batches.

maria.sre: observing metrics after shift: errors dropping from 18% -> 4% over 6m, p95 latency slowly recovering.

priya.support: updated ACME ticket SUP-1423 with mitigation steps and asked if they can test again. also flagged potential billing noise: customers with automated retry loops may see increased token usage due to reconnects. asked billing to watch spikes.

kevin.neteng: provider confirmed they swapped to backup aggregation at 08:40 and will run fiber diagnostics; they suspect microbursts from a misconfigured MPLS buffer profile on one vendor box. NOC will provide RCA.

maria.sre: filing an incident page and will start postmortem once RCA comes in. immediate action items:
- (maria) finalize incident timeline and collect tcpdumps/metric windows
- (kevin) follow up with provider and obtain BGP/PE logs
- (sam) land soft-retry change and add circuit-aware backoff
- (priya) coordinate customer comms and billing watch

alex.infra: temporary policy left in place until provider confirms stable (will revert after 24h).

priya.support: ACME confirmed reduced disconnects after 09:02 UTC. they requested a short writeup for their compliance team.

maria.sre: thanks all. tagging for follow-up: we need a postmortem template entry for "provider microburst leading to connection resets and upstream 502s; caused cascading auth/timeouts and customer streaming disruption".

kevin.neteng: saved NOC ticket TG-789 and provider ticket PT-482 for postmortem.

sam.runtime: I'll also add a small server-side enhancement to detect repeated mid-stream RSTs and surface clearer error codes to clients (avoid generic 502).

maria.sre: closing active ping phase — moving incident to 'monitor' state. will update when RCA received. :white_check_mark:
